2. For each character grep all the words in which the character is

For example:
for key "a" the values could be "and", "bad", "amazon" etc

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] GREP application on Hadoop using RHIPE
parts:
Hi,
First of , don't use rhlapply. It has been removed and was the distributed
version of lapply - so it did not take any input folder (as far as i recall), if
it did it would only take sequence file input format not text file.

For your problem below, use rhmr, specifying the input folder with text files
and use text/sequence output format.

> 1. Sequence along the characters from "a" to "z",which are my keys.
> 2. For each character grep all the words in which the character is
> appearing. For this i am using R grep() function. These vector of
> words would be my "values" to the keys.
> For example:
>  for key "a" the values could be "and", "bad", "amazon" etc
> for key "b" the values could be "bad", "boss" etc.. (Note there would
> be duplication of words)
>

So your map would look like

map <- expression({
lines.of.text <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values),"[[:space:]]+"))
counts <- sapply(letters,function(alpha){
value <- lines.of.text[grep(alpha, lines.of.text)]
if(length(value)==0) value <- ''
rhcollect(alpha,value)
})
})

mapred <- list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0, mapred.field.separator="
",mapred.job.tracker='local')
z <- rhmr(map=map, ifolder=path-to-input,ofolder="/tmp/job",
inout=c("text","text"),mapred=mapred)
rhex(z)

(You need the if(length(value)==0 bit, for text output. RHIPE throws an
indexoutofbounds exception when trying to strinfigy a vector of length 0. For
sequence file output, it is not needed, the return value be an empty
character vector)

Hope this helps

Saptarshi

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] GREP application on Hadoop using RHIPE
parts:
I should also point out that those values (vectors) could potentially
be very large!

Since you already have a case where you might get multiple lines for
the same key( since each
map task will potentially write a value for the key 'a' and there is
no reducer), you
might as well split long values and write them out as multiple lines.
RHIPE has a cap on value length i think its 128MB or 256MB.

The following code doesn't do that. It instead, partitions by key
(values for same letter in one file) and sorts within part file (by
key)

map <- expression({
lines.of.text <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values),"[[:space:]]+"))
counts <- sapply(letters,function(alpha){
value <- lines.of.text[grep(alpha, lines.of.text)]
if(length(value)==0) value <- ''
rhcollect(alpha,value)
})
})

reduce <- expression(
reduce = { lapply(reduce.values,function(r) rhcollect(reduce.key,r)) }
)

mapred <- list(mapred.field.separator=" ")
z <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce, ifolder=filename,ofolder="/tmp/job",
inout=c("text","text"),orderby="char",mapred=mapred,part=list(lims=1,type='string'))
rhex(z)

This can take time, e.g. for 2.8GB data read (100MM records, 5 words
per line), 14GB was written (867,984 records)
and it took 13 minutes (72 cores, 8 computers, 5 TB of space)

BTW, the reducer is an identity reducer, but if you use the 'orderby'
parameter, you *have* to provide an R reducer.
Saptarshi

For this example, you don't need the orderby. Byte ordering for single
characters is the same as letter ordering (and faster - i think).
If you don't use orderby, you can skip the reducer code.

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: GREP application on Hadoop using RHIPE
parts:
I think you're using the rhcollect in a manner different from what you intended.

rhgetkey is used as:

rhgetkey(list(key1,key2,...)),...)

so key is equal to something like this (the way you've used it)
list(k=letters[i],v=grep(letters[i],map.values,value=TRUE))

for some i, and so on.

Maybe you want :

rhcollect(letters[i], grep(letters[i],map.values,value=TRUE))

then you can do rhgetkey(list("a"), ....)

Saptarshi

> rhS2M function is not recognized function) but i am getting the
> error.

There isn't an rhS2M function. You are reading an old help manual. See 0.65.2.

Q1: What the is output of rhread(..., max=1) ( specify the input
folder for the sequence file output, not the map file output).
I would like to see your keys.


If you have a reducer, the number of output files is the number of
reduce tasks. If you do not have a reducer
the number of output files is the number of map tasks.
The number of map tasks depends on the size of your file(s). The
number of reduce tasks can be specified by you.
But for 26 keys, it's not going to more than 26.

messages.subject: Re: GREP application on Hadoop using RHIPE
parts:
Hello,

Not surprising. The map potentially emits multiple records for a given letter of
the alphabet (key). So your part files have multiple records for a key.

Using map file output format won't help you in this case (you'll only get the
first).

1. Compute a count of the number of records for a given letter of the alphabet.
   map --> (letter[i], 1)
   reduce ---> expression(
         pre = { total <- 0 },
         reduce = { total <- total+ sum(unlist(reduce.values)) },
         post = { rhcollect(reduce.key, total) }
    )

2. Also, using partitioner=list(lims=1, type='string') and
   mapred.reduce.tasks=27 will create 27 part files, each key (letter of the
   alphabet) being places in its own table.


Saptarshi

Why are you writing your own identity reducer? It is only required (identity) when using

You will get 26 files,  but the map outputformat does not work with either of

a) orderby
b) parts

Reason: 
a) orderby changes the ordering of the output data. Information regarding this new ordering is
not made available to the MapFileI.Reader thingummy. Wont work. No plans of making it work.
b) parts: Parts uses a different hashcode generating algorithm which is not exposed to the MapFile.Reader
Both of these change how the keys are sorted and partitioned. But the final data set does not contain information
about these different sorting/partitioning schemes and uses the default one (which wont work).

No plan of changing this.

I interpret this as "different values for same key scattered across multiple files"
By design, all values for a key are sent to one part file (Hadoop MapReduce design),
so no, they are not scattered across multiple part files.
